entries.title: II Kings 4:1
segments: The power to take and hold men as bondmen in payment for debt, is a source of great distress, from which all proper means should be used to afford relief.

entries.title: II Kings 4:7
segments: Poverty does not release debtors from obligation to pay their creditors.  Whenever God gives them the means to pay their debts, they should do it with promptness and alacrity.

entries.title: II Kings 4:8
segments:
Shunem; a city in the tribe of Issachar. 
 
  A great woman; wealthy and influential.

entries.title: II Kings 4:9
segments: A disposition to relieve and assist the pious is pecularily pleasing to God, and a means of securing the special manifestations of his presence and favor.

entries.title: II Kings 4:13
segments: The truly pious are grateful for the favors they receive, and are disposed to make the best return in their power.

entries.title: II Kings 4:18
segments: Some of the highest joys and the deepest sorrows come to parents through the medium of their children.  But both are from God, and in both he should be acknowledged as doing all things well.

entries.title: II Kings 4:26
segments: True piety inspires a deep interest in the happiness of others, especially of benefactors; and leads us to delight in communicating enjoyment, as we have opportunity, to all, especially to the people of God.

entries.title: II Kings 4:27
segments: The Lord hath hid it from me, and hath not told me; the prophets did not know more than other men, except as the Lord taught them.

entries.title: II Kings 4:38
segments:
A dearth; scarcity of food. 
 
  Seethe; boil.

entries.title: II Kings 4:39
segments:
Knew--not; that they were hurtful. 
 
Though every creature of God is good for the purpose for which he made it, yet there are many things which he did not make for food or drink; and men cannot so use them without producing sickness and death, and, if they know these to be their effects, sinning against God.

entries.title: II Kings 4:40
segments: Death; that which was hurtful and might cause death.

entries.title: II Kings 4:41
segments: No harm; nothing that would injure them.

entries.title: II Kings 4:42
segments:
Baal-shalisha; in the tribe of Ephraim. 
 
Kindness to the good because they are good blesses not only those who bestow and those who receive it, but often multitudes of others; and while it breathes goodwill to men, it brings glory in the highest to God.
